question: A master has the sound of a programme and where it is, and no field for what a stream says of the programme as a whole: how loud its dialogue is, which downmix to two channels it prefers and at what levels, which DRC profiles it was made with. The plan of the round had a side report of these for the encoder of a second generation, to be kept if a second generation then said them again, and left it. What does a second generation say of them when its encoder is told nothing, can the encoders be told, and does it come back when they are?
method: Two things had to be so first. The downmix a stream says was not reported at all, and is since evidence 58. And an encoder had to take a dialogue normalisation by hand: the help of the E-AC-3 encoder names `measure_only` and nothing else for `--loudness-management`, and evidence 54 was read as if that were all; it was asked here, and takes `skip:custom_dialnorm=` as the TrueHD encoder says it does. `tools/encoder_arguments.py` reads a stream with `oadec info`, `emdf` and `oamd` and writes what it says as the arguments the encoders take, for a field of which the stream says one thing from its first frame to its last. `tools/interop.py programme` then asks whether it comes back: four scenes of the round-trip design (rows 8, 15, 34 and 44), each encoded three times with a programme that is not the encoder's defaults (three downmixes and pairs of DRC profiles, two of them with a dialogue normalisation given by hand, one with the measured one), all at 768 kbit/s; each first stream decoded to a master with `--warp-mode stream`; and the master encoded twice, once with the encoder told nothing and once with it told the arguments read of the first stream. What each of the 36 streams says is read with the same commands and laid side by side, field by field.
commands: oadec decode --format damf --warp-mode stream -o <base> <first.ec3>; oadec info|emdf|oamd --json <stream>

oadec.name: oadec-downmix-2.exe
oadec.what: the binary that reports the downmix (evidence 58)

dolby: Dolby Media Encoder: dee_ddpjoc_encoder and dee_dthd_encoder of the Dolby Encoding Engine 5.7.2

a_dialogue_normalisation_given_by_hand.without_a_value_the_e_ac_3_encoder_says: Failed to parse 'loudness-management'. Required option: 'custom_dialnorm' not found.

whole_tracks_of_streaming_services.what: whole tracks of streaming services, E-AC-3 with JOC at 768 kbit/s, none of them of the corpus
left_to_the_encoder: the downmix: the stream says none

what_is_left_to_an_encoder: a field of which the stream says two things, as a splice of two programmes does
the DRC profile of a TrueHD stream, which says none: only the gains one led to
a downmix for the TrueHD encoder, which has no option for one
a surround level the stream says with a code the tables reserve

tests.python tools/encoder_arguments.py --self: 12 of 12 known answers, without a stream
tests.python tools/interop.py --self-check: three more known answers: a second stream held to the first field by field, the count, and the settings

reading: Told nothing, the encoder of a second generation writes a programme of its own: of twelve first streams the second says the dialogue normalisation of the first in 3, its preferred downmix in 0, the levels of the downmix in 0, the DRC profile of line mode in 0 and of RF mode in 0; the warp mode, which a master has a place for and the decode was told to keep, in 12. Told what `tools/encoder_arguments.py` reads of the first stream, it says all six as the first did, twelve of twelve, and every one of the 36 streams is clean. So the side report the plan asked for is kept, as a tool beside the decoder and not as a file the decoder writes: `info`, `emdf` and `oamd` already report everything it needs, once `info` had the downmix. Both encoders take a dialogue normalisation by hand, the E-AC-3 one without saying so in its help, and write the value they are told. It has a price that the arguments cannot avoid: an encoder that is told one measures nothing, so the loudness payloads of the stream hold the figure it was given and no true peak, 0 streams of twelve against 12 where the encoder measured. Whoever wants the measurement gives the encoder the `--encoder` part alone. Read the same way, 4 whole tracks of streaming services, 8.6 hours that are not of the corpus, each say one dialogue normalisation throughout, the same two DRC profiles and the Lo/Ro warp mode, and none says a downmix: there the tool tells the encoder the first three and leaves it the fourth, in words.
